title: ESPN and College Football Playoff in tense media-rights negotiations with Oct. 9 deadline
dek: ESPN and the College Football Playoff are in difficult negotiations on media rights for a 24-team playoff expansion. The core issue: any deal must exceed the $250 million in aggregate revenue that FBS conference championship games currently generate. An Oct. 9 deadline marks the end of ESPN's exclusive negotiating window.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The CFP and ESPN have an Oct. 9 deadline to strike a deal; if they fail, CFP media rights go to open market where Fox, NBC, and Prime Video could bid.
bottom_line: October 9 is when ESPN's exclusive bargaining window closes. If the sides remain apart on how to value 24 playoff games against lost conference championship revenue, the CFP moves to open market, a shift that could reshape the broadcast landscape and force ESPN to compete against rivals it has locked out of college football for decades.
body: The ESPN and the College Football Playoff are in difficult negotiations over media rights for a 24-team playoff expansion, with a core disagreement over revenue threatening to derail a deal by an October 9 deadline.

In September, CFP leadership formally opened a 30-day exclusive negotiating window with current rights-holder ESPN, per Awful Announcing. That window expires October 9. According to Austin Karp of Sports Business Journal, the conversations between ESPN and its conference partners have been tough sledding regarding a potential new CFP deal that reflects the expected 24-team expansion, per Awful Announcing reporting.

The central hurdle is financial. FBS conference championship games currently generate approximately $250 million in aggregate revenue, with the SEC Championship Game alone valued at around $100 million for the conference, per Awful Announcing. Any deal for a 24-team playoff would need to exceed that $250 million figure for the conferences, otherwise expansion would not make financial sense, per the outlet.

If ESPN and the CFP do not reach agreement before October 9, the rights for the expanded postseason would go to open market, at which point Fox, NBC, Prime Video, or other potential broadcasters could submit bids, per Awful Announcing. For the CFP, taking its rights to market and potentially splitting inventory into multiple packages sold to multiple broadcasters represents its best chance of generating the value necessary to make a 24-team playoff worth it, according to Awful Announcing.

ESPN still has eight days remaining to submit an offer compelling enough to convince the CFP to stick with the outlet on an exclusive basis, per Awful Announcing. Should no agreement occur by October 9, the CFP will have until December 1 to strike a new deal in time for expansion in the 2027 season, according to Awful Announcing.
